uncertainties.note: Speakers untagged. 1594 names the opponent as the Blue Hawk (Meio Plato's locked nickname), so 1590/1593 (formal first person, 'coming after me') are read as that opponent's reply to the shouts in 1589/1591/1592; 1590 and 1593 are identical text with different wait values. No speaker names were written into the English.
'Te-awase' (a bout / trying one's skill against someone) rendered as 'face you in combat'; the speaker is an enemy ace addressing Amuro (White Devil) but is not identified in the table.
Ship damage reports at the end of resource 6043; the ship is not named in these rows (1583 only says 'Captain'). Left unnamed.

Source says roughly 'so those are that group?' (rei no renchuu: the group both parties already know about). English 'the ones I heard about' supplies a mild 'I heard'; alternative: 'So those are the ones?'. 1620 ('I've heard about you all') supports it. Continuation of 1607, same speaker.

SOF dai-ichi kidou butai no moto chief: rendered 'former chief of the SOF 1st Mobile Unit'. Eureka Seven wiki describes Holland as a former SOF unit/platoon leader; exact English unit name is not attested. See proposals file.
Exchange read as the Frost brothers (1624 addresses an older brother; Shagia/Olba named in 1683 and 1731). Which brother says 1621-1623 is not settled by the table; English stays neutral.

Nine near-identical 'base captured' voice variants. 1632 and 1633 differ in source only by a particle; English variation between them is cosmetic. 1634 has no subject in source; passive used rather than 'we'.
zenmetsu vs kaimetsu both mean the escort force is lost; rendered 'wiped out' / 'destroyed' to keep the variants distinct.
'Captain' here is the loanword used aboard the Freeden for Jamil (1659 addresses Garrod in the same voice), but the table does not tag it; English just says 'Captain'.
Sentence-final 'ka' read as rueful realisation ('so it's a failure'), not a real question.
Source omits who 'can do something like this' (follows the all-bases-captured report). Kept passive.
Subject (Holland, from 1663) omitted in source; English keeps it subjectless.
87 visible characters with <ab(500)>: fits the 110 limit but is long for the display time.
